findings.defect: The new policy grants the Total Architect power to approve and merge bounded non-Foundation work without asking Owner, but it never names an acceptance authority and never says that authority must be other than the Builder/authoring pass. Master Blueprint invariant 13 allows autonomous merge only when the delegated policy explicitly defines bounded scope, acceptance authority, and no-self-certification controls. Gate 8 requires Class S/D/O acceptance to be Owner or an Owner-designated approver that is not the Builder seat, and says a delegated merge policy must name that authority. The preservation clause only says a material authoring pass cannot use its own output as independent review evidence. The scope section says the Total Architect does not become a second Owner, while the delegated-authority bullets give that same seat approval. The law-router insert authorizes delegated approval for non-Foundation work without restating the non-Builder rule.
findings.consequence: A fresh AUTO seat can treat itself as both Builder and approver for any work it labels non-Foundation, then merge that work. That is self-certification of material work, which invariant 11, Gate 8, Class O, the AUTO no-self-certification section, and bootstrap section 8 forbid. Because acceptance authority is unnamed, the policy also fails the precondition invariant 13 sets for delegated merge.
findings.smallest_repair: Replace 'approve and merge' with merge execution only after the task's recorded acceptance_authority has already accepted that exact head. Name the authority: Owner, or for Class O only an Owner-designated approver that is not the Builder/authoring pass. State that the Total Architect authoring pass cannot be that approver.

findings.defect: Preserved separation says independent review, when required by law/task, must remain 'independently sourced or separately evidenced.' The 'or' makes a separate evidence artifact an alternative to an independent source. 'When required' lets the executing seat decide the review is not required. The next bullet then says CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM findings are Owner-dispositioned only 'where current law requires Owner authority,' which is narrower than Foundation Law and Blueprint text that CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM findings may be repaired or explicitly rejected only by Owner.
findings.consequence: A fresh seat can satisfy 'required independent evidence' with a second record from the authoring pass, skip review by classifying the task as not requiring it, and disposition its own material findings. That weakens no-self-certification and the independent-review gate the operating model still lists before governed merge.
findings.smallest_repair: Delete 'or separately evidenced' and the 'where current law requires Owner authority' qualifier. Require that when independent review applies, the reviewer pass is not the authoring pass and is not evidence for itself. Keep CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM rejection as Owner-only, matching Foundation Law and Blueprint section 13.

findings.defect: For every Owner-reserved gate, including final Foundation and Master Blueprint acceptance, the policy says Owner may decide in the current chat and the Total Architect must then record the durable acceptance, bind the exact target, and merge. It also tells the Total Architect to record an Owner acceptance comment and to relay 'equivalent' exact-head acceptance text. Nothing requires the Owner utterance itself to name the candidate commit SHA, nothing requires a verbatim quote, and binding the SHA is a later mechanical step performed by the Total Architect. The anti-fabrication clause only forbids inventing an acceptance or inferring one from silence. It does not forbid paraphrase or post-hoc SHA attachment. Canonical practice on protected main records Owner acceptance against an accepted exact head inside the Owner decision itself. Current state still blocks Foundation final acceptance on Owner, with acceptance_authority OWNER.
findings.consequence: A fresh seat can turn a chat utterance that does not identify a commit into a GitHub/durable 'Owner acceptance' of a head the Owner did not name, then merge that head. Later seats will treat the Total Architect's equivalent record as canonical Owner acceptance because chat is non-canonical until durably recorded. That weakens the ban on fabricated Owner acceptance, exact-head fail-closed merge, and Foundation/Master Blueprint final Owner acceptance, which invariant 13 says a delegated policy must not weaken.
findings.smallest_repair: For reserved gates, allow a durable acceptance only as a verbatim quote of an Owner utterance that already contains the full candidate commit SHA, plus packet blob SHA when a packet is in scope. Delete 'equivalent.' If the utterance has no SHA, or the head changes after it, fail closed and do not bind a new SHA. Merge only when that quoted SHA is still the PR head and the required checks are on that same SHA.

findings.defect: Delegated merge is defined by a negative list: bounded non-Foundation work, plus routine operational/state/documentation transitions that do not alter constitutional objectives, Foundation invariants, law precedence, canonical-authority topology, or role-separation rules. Class S is non-Foundation and still requires a non-Builder acceptance and, when it touches canonical state, schemas, or core interfaces, independent review. Class F includes Master Blueprint text, canonical authority, and role powers, not only the five excluded phrases. Routine state transitions include state/current.yaml and state/tasks.yaml, which are canonical operational authorities. The reserved-gate list omits the still-active AUTO stops for enabling autonomous merge, choosing among materially different foundation designs, expanding beyond the approved objective, and accepting unresolved material risk that is not Foundation risk. The AUTO file points merge execution at the new policy ('governed by') but does not explicitly supersede the stop 'enabling autonomous merge.' The new policy also says AUTO may execute everything current law and the Master Blueprint permit. Foundation Law requires explicit supersession for a same-level conflict; Blueprint conflict resolution says to prefer newer text only when same-level supersession is explicit, otherwise fail closed.
findings.consequence: Two fresh-seat readings both cause harm. The open reading treats the new policy as the merge governor and merges Class S work, non-freeze Blueprint or law edits, and canonical state/task gate changes as routine, including while Foundation acceptance is still blocked. The closed reading sees an unresolved conflict with the unsuperseded autonomous-merge stop and cannot tell which rule wins. Either way the policy does not keep one bounded Class O lane, and it can move protected-main canonical state without the Owner gate the current task registry still records.
findings.smallest_repair: Add one explicit carve-out: delegated merge is only clerical merge of an already-accepted Class O exact head and is not a general enablement of autonomous merge. Exclude Class F, Class S, Master Blueprint edits, law-router edits, role-power edits, and state/task mutations that change phase, acceptance_authority, next action, or the Foundation gate. Restate the omitted AUTO stops as still binding. Delete 'AUTO may execute everything those authorities permit.'

independence_statement: Fresh independent read-only review; no prior MINH TRÍ chat conclusions used as authority.
